skill.name: dispatching-parallel-agents
skill.description: Guides developers to split independent debugging or implementation work across focused parallel AI agents.
skill.summary: Dispatch independent coding tasks to focused parallel agents, then review and integrate their results.
skill.author: sickn33

content.value_statement: Sequential debugging slows teams when failures are independent. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to split work into focused parallel agent tasks.
actual_capabilities: Helps identify independent problem domains before dispatching agents.
Provides a pattern for one focused agent task per subsystem or test file.
Shows how to write constrained prompts with clear goals and expected output.
Explains when parallel work is unsafe because tasks share state or context.
Guides review, conflict checks, full test runs, and final integration.
limitations: Works only when tasks are truly independent.
Does not execute agents or manage tool sessions by itself.
Requires human review before merging results from multiple agents.
Is not suited for broad exploratory debugging or shared-state failures.

use_cases.title: Split failing test files
use_cases.description: Assign separate agents to unrelated test files so each investigation stays focused.

use_cases.title: Coordinate subsystem fixes
use_cases.description: Route independent subsystem bugs to separate agents while keeping integration review centralized.

use_cases.title: Plan agent workloads
use_cases.description: Convert a mixed issue list into scoped prompts with constraints and expected summaries.

prompt_templates.title: Find parallel work
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these failures and group them by independent problem domain. Tell me which groups can be assigned to parallel agents and why.

prompt_templates.title: Create focused tasks
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn these independent problem groups into focused agent tasks. Each task should include scope, goal, constraints, and expected summary.

prompt_templates.title: Dispatch safely
prompt_templates.scenario: Avoid overlap before starting parallel work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check these proposed agent tasks for shared files, shared state, or sequencing risks. Revise them so parallel work is safe.

prompt_templates.title: Integrate results
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these agent summaries and proposed changes. Identify conflicts, missing validation, and the final integration order.

output_examples.input: Three unrelated test files fail after a refactor.
output_examples.output: The skill would group each test file as a separate domain, assign one focused agent per file, and require full-suite verification afterward.

output_examples.input: Two failures touch the same shared service.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend a single investigation first, because parallel agents could make conflicting changes.

output_examples.input: An agent returns a fix summary after working on one subsystem.
output_examples.output: The skill would prompt review of the summary, changed files, conflict risk, and tests before integrating the work.

best_practices: Dispatch agents only after confirming the work has independent scope.
Give each agent one clear goal, concrete constraints, and expected output.
Review every summary and run the full validation suite before integration.
anti_patterns: Do not assign parallel agents to related failures that may share one root cause.
Do not use vague prompts such as asking an agent to fix everything.
Do not integrate parallel changes without conflict checks and validation.

faq.question: Does this skill run multiple agents automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides a planning and review pattern for tools that support agent dispatch.

faq.question: When should I avoid this skill?
faq.answer: Avoid it when failures are related, require shared context, or touch the same mutable state.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is written for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: What makes a good agent task?
faq.answer: A good task has one scope, a clear goal, useful context, constraints, and a requested summary.

faq.question: How should I handle agent results?
faq.answer: Read each summary, inspect changes, check conflicts, and run the relevant tests plus the full suite.

faq.question: Is this only for test failures?
faq.answer: No. It also applies to independent bugs or implementation tasks across separate subsystems.
